timing.speedup_note: Apparent 38% speedup in mean time/experiment vs. prior milestone (22.7 → 14.0 min). Partially attributable to fast-fail blocked experiments (no live GPU) rather than genuine GPU throughput gains.

slowest_experiments.description: Exp 219: Live GSM8K semantic benchmark on Qwen3.5-0.8B and Gemma
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Sequential single-GPU inference with no DualGPURunner, no model pre-warm, cold-start load stall absorbed into experiment wall time. Z3 constraint calls were also sequential with no per-call timeout.

slowest_experiments.description: Exp 308: JEPA fast-path gate integration (tests failing — checkpoint)
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Failure recovery triggered full 6500-test suite rerun on each fix iteration instead of targeted module-level reruns. Each rerun took ~8 minutes, and the fix required 3–4 iterations.

slowest_experiments.description: Exp 184: 3B model verification — does verify-repair help large models
slowest_experiments.root_cause: 3B model loaded on single GPU without pre-warm; lazy CUDA initialization stall not separated from inference timing. No batched inference; questions sent one at a time.

slowest_experiments.description: Exp 221: Live prompt-side constraint benchmark on typed IR tasks
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Sequential inference with per-question Z3 calls and no per-call timeout. One malformed constraint caused Z3 to spin for >10 minutes before the outer loop timed out.

slowest_experiments.description: Exp 155: Retrain JEPA violation predictor v2 with multi-domain data
slowest_experiments.root_cause: CPU training of full JEPA model on multi-domain dataset without batching or early-stopping heuristic. No checkpoint-resume, so a mid-run crash required a full restart from epoch 0.

gpu_utilization.zombie_note: PID 3378630 holds 25 GB VRAM across both GPUs with 0% GPU utilization (wall time 2019s, CPU 484s). This is a zombie model process — model loaded but inference loop exited, CUDA context not released. Represents ~1 GB wasted every 30 seconds of idle conductor time.

idle_cause_breakdown.sequential_inference_no_dual_runner: ~25% idle time — model A ran while GPU 1 sat empty
idle_cause_breakdown.cold_start_stalls: ~15% idle time — lazy CUDA init not pre-warmed
idle_cause_breakdown.carnot_force_live_not_propagating: ~15% idle time — conductor subprocesses ran simulated paths, GPU never used
idle_cause_breakdown.zombie_processes_between_experiments: ~5% idle time — VRAM locked, GC not triggered

zombie_processes.action_required: Kill PID 3378630 to recover 25 GB VRAM before next conductor session. Run: kill 3378630
zombie_processes.prevention: gpu_monitor.py --kill-zombies should be invoked by conductor at experiment teardown, not just at startup. Currently only called once at session start.

parallelization_opportunities.approach: Auto-wire DualGPURunner for any experiment specifying >1 model variant. GPU 0 runs model A, GPU 1 runs model B concurrently. Wall time cut by ~50% for 2-model comparisons.
CPU training (EORM/JEPA retrain) can run on GPU 0 while GPU 1 handles independent benchmark inference. These have no data dependency.
Group all Z3 calls for a question batch, run in a subprocess pool with per-call 30s timeout. Eliminates single-constraint hangs from blocking the full experiment.
Reconcile spec.md + traceability.md + status.md + changelog.md in a single batch write at experiment end rather than four sequential file reads and writes.

bottlenecks_identified: No per-experiment hard timeout in conductor: Exp 219 ran 117 min with no kill signal. A 45-minute hard cap would have freed the GPU 72 minutes earlier.
DualGPURunner not auto-wired: dual-model benchmarks (219, 221, 184) each ran sequentially on one GPU while the second sat idle. No conductor policy to detect this pattern.

CARNOT_FORCE_LIVE env var not propagating to conductor subprocesses: five consecutive milestones produced only simulated GPU results. Root cause fixed in Exp 352/377, but the fix requires an online GPU node at session start.

Full test suite reruns on targeted failures: Exp 308 re-ran the 6500-test suite 3–4 times during failure debugging. Targeted `pytest tests/python/test_experiment_308*.py` would have cut debugging time by ~70%.

No model pre-warm before timed inference: cold CUDA init (20–45s) was absorbed into experiment wall time for Exps 155, 184, 219. ExperimentTemplate.setup_gpu() exists but was not called in pre-template experiments.
CPU training without checkpoint-resume: Exp 155 restart from epoch 0 after crash cost ~40 minutes. ExperimentTemplate.checkpoint_save() exists but was not used.
Zombie GPU processes between experiments: PID 3378630 held 25 GB VRAM with 0% utilization. gpu_monitor --kill-zombies only called at session start, not at experiment teardown.

Doc reconciliation not batched: each experiment updated 4–6 ops files sequentially. Conductor made ~2400 file-write operations across the milestone that could be reduced by 60% with a single end-of-experiment batch write.
Interrupted sessions without state recovery: Exps 378, 386, 387 were missing from milestone close. No automatic conductor state checkpoint allowed resuming from the last completed experiment.
improvements_suggested: Add conductor hard timeout: 45 minutes per experiment, configurable per experiment type. Emit RETRO entry and continue on timeout rather than hanging.
Auto-detect dual-model experiments and wire DualGPURunner: if an experiment spec lists >1 LLM variant, the conductor should schedule GPU 0 / GPU 1 in parallel automatically.

Enforce pre-warm before timed inference: conductor should call ExperimentTemplate.setup_gpu() for any experiment with requires_gpu=True. Fail fast if pre-warm fails rather than timing stalled inference.
Targeted test reruns on failure: conductor should run only the failing module's test file on each fix iteration. Full suite rerun only on final pass before marking experiment complete.
Enforce checkpoint-resume in all training experiments: conductor should verify that checkpoint_save() is called at least once per training loop epoch batch before allowing long-running CPU training.
Kill zombie GPU processes at experiment teardown: add gpu_monitor --kill-zombies to conductor post-experiment hook, not just session startup.
Batch doc reconciliation: write a single reconcile_docs() call at experiment end that updates all ops files in one pass. Reduces I/O from ~6 sequential writes to 1 batched write.
Conductor state checkpoint on interrupt: serialize the conductor's experiment queue and completed-set to a JSON file on SIGINT/SIGTERM so sessions can resume without re-running completed experiments.
Add per-call Z3 timeout (30s default): wrap all Z3 solver invocations in a subprocess with a configurable timeout. Log timed-out constraints to a debug file rather than blocking.

GPU node health check at conductor session start: if CARNOT_FORCE_LIVE=1 and no GPU is available, emit a critical alert and pause rather than silently running simulated paths for the entire milestone.

savings_breakdown.note: Savings are additive estimates assuming all improvements implemented simultaneously. Actual savings will vary based on experiment mix in next milestone.

retro_items_open.description: Conductor lacks per-experiment hard timeout — runaway experiments block the queue.
GPU node offline for fifth consecutive milestone — CARNOT_FORCE_LIVE=1 set correctly but no live GPU available.
CIKAN not implemented — cikan_energy.py is still JSON stub after two consecutive milestone failures.
FR-11 relay running synthetic-only for third consecutive milestone.

retro_items_closed_this_milestone.description: LiveGPUGate infrastructure fix applied in Exp 377. CARNOT_FORCE_LIVE=1 now exported correctly in session_startup.sh. Remaining gap: GPU node must be online.

what_went_well: Mean time per experiment fell from 22.7 to 14.0 minutes (38% apparent improvement).
ExperimentTemplate adoption eliminated cold-start boilerplate for all new experiments.
RETRO-015 infrastructure fix was correct on first attempt.
115-test suite for Exp 389 retro script maintained 100% targeted coverage.
what_went_poorly: Five consecutive milestones without a single live GPU result — the most critical research gap.
Interrupted sessions (Exps 378, 386, 387) left RETRO-020 and RETRO-021 unresolved for a third time.
Zombie GPU process (PID 3378630) consuming 25 GB VRAM at milestone close — resource leak not caught by existing monitoring.
Full test suite reruns on targeted failures remain the dominant per-experiment time sink.
process_improvements_for_next_milestone: Before starting the next milestone, kill PID 3378630 and verify GPU node is online (nvidia-smi + CARNOT_FORCE_LIVE=1 smoke test).
Prioritize RETRO-020 (CIKAN) and RETRO-019 (GPU online) as P0 before any new capability experiments.
Add conductor hard timeout as the first infrastructure experiment of the next milestone — this is RETRO-003 and has been carried 15+ milestones.
